units.translation: 256-59. Would that Phrixus too: for it is said that when Helle fell, the ram, by the will of Zeus, spoke to the anxious Phrixus, encouraging him that it would bring him safely to Scythia. This very thing was destined to become an evil for Alcimede, since her son was sent there. The story is found in Hecataeus (1 fr. 17 J.), that the ram spoke. But some say that he sailed on a ram-prowed vessel. Dionysius in his second book (32 fr. 2b J.) says that Crius was Phrixus' foster-father and sailed with him to Colchis; for this reason the story of the ram's sacrifice there was mythologized.

260. At the entrance: at the exit of the nobles; from 'to go forward'. Hence they also call the first approaches of mountains 'entrances'.

262-63a. 〈Stricken:〉 harmed by grief or dispirited. Lg
b. Sharp for each: it is transferred from things pertaining to touch, as
28 μετενήνεκται in F : -ενήνοχεν in L : -ηνέχθη in P
in Homer (Λ 269): 'as when a sharp dart holds a woman in labor'. Grief is a confusion of the soul, intense pain; this is clear from the poet saying (ο 358): 'she wasted away with grief for her son'.

264. Wrapped in bed: tightly bound, so that all the limbs are impressed from the constriction. 'Wrapped' is also said of one who has covered his face in such a way that the outline is seen through the cloak.
